turns.content: An eight-carbon disubstituted aromatic compound contains a carbonyl group and an aryl-halogen bond. Determine the aromatic proton count and enumerate plausible two-carbon side chains for the nonhalogen substituent.
A benzene ring uses six of the eight carbons. Use that carbon accounting to refine the candidate side chains identified in the first step.

For the candidate that places an Ar-CH2 group next to a one-proton downfield site, determine whether signals at 3.7 and 9.9 ppm could both be independent singlets; include the expected vicinal coupling.
The aromatic region contains doublets at 7.8 and 7.6 ppm, each integrating to two protons. What substitution symmetry does that pattern support?
Which integration and splitting evidence most cleanly distinguishes the two side-chain classes developed above?
Apply that test to a proposal with 9.9 ppm (1H, s) and 3.7 ppm (2H, s), and compare it with one containing 2.3 ppm (3H, s).
State the complete best-supported proton-NMR pattern, including shifts, integrations, and multiplicities.
Qualify the assignment in light of missing coupling constants, resolution, purity information, mixture analysis, and independent structural confirmation.
Check the assignment against aromatic integration, the eight-carbon total, and the coupling expected between any adjacent methylene and one-proton downfield site.
Report the final proton-NMR pattern and the most plausible structural class.
